needsBespoke.why: Thunderclap's kit combines an armor-scaling stat-conversion (bonus armor feeds W and E damage via armor ratios) with an empowered-attack that also triggers a distinct, separately-timed cone on-hit rider for a different duration (6s empowered-attack window vs 5s cone-splash window) and an attack-reset — no single closed-list primitive captures the combination of 'armor is itself a damage-scaling stat fed by a self-buff whose magnitude is tripled by a shield state' plus the two-tier empowered-attack/on-hit-cone structure with independent timers. The simulator needs bespoke logic to: (1) track Malphite's armor stat live (base+bonus+item armor, further increased by the passive itself and its own W rank), (2) apply the tripled multiplier only while Granite Shield (a defensive proc-based shield) is currently up, and (3) manage two separate expiring windows (empowered-attack-arm at 6s, cone-active at 5s) stacked on the attack-reset behavior.

proposal: Pre-fight: assume Granite Shield is up (dummy never damages Malphite), so Thunderclap's passive bonus armor is tripled for the whole fight.
Open with Ground Slam (E) on cooldown for its high magic damage-to-armor/AP scaling and short 7s cooldown.
Cast Thunderclap (W) to arm the empowered basic attack, then immediately auto-attack to consume the empowerment (also resets attack timer) and to start the on-hit cone window.
Cast Seismic Shard (Q) on cooldown for magic damage (its slow/speed-steal is not relevant to the dummy fight).

Keep auto-attacking throughout to benefit from the 5s on-hit cone splash window after each Thunderclap cast, refreshing Thunderclap on cooldown to re-arm the empowered attack and reset the attack timer again.
Cast Unstoppable Force (R) once available (100/115/130s cooldown, likely only usable once near the start of a 15s fight if at all) for its large magic burst.
Continue looping E > W(+auto) > Q on cooldown, weaving in basic attacks between casts, prioritizing whichever ability comes off cooldown first to minimize downtime, subject to mana budget.
questions: In the damage fight's ~15s window with likely level 16-18 CDR-less base cooldowns, will Malphite realistically ever get to cast R (100-130s CD) at all, or should R be excluded from the rotation entirely?
Should the rotation assume max mana (or infinite mana) is provided, given Q+W+E costs could exceed a fresh Malphite's mana pool well before 15s elapses?

Does the simulator model auto-attacks between spell casts at all, or does it only count declared abilities — if autos are excluded, does Thunderclap's active even deal its w_3/w_4 damage in this framework?

Should the opening sequence prioritize maximizing early single large-cooldown casts (R, E) or maximize total auto-attack uptime with W's empowerment, given W's cooldown (8-10s) is much shorter than the empowered-attack arm window (6s) and cone window (5s)?
